evidence.excerpt:
Once historical clients become unavailable, a federation
must serve newcomers through the artifact it leaves behind.
How much of its knowledge remains useful in an architec-
ture chosen afterward? We introduceFEDNBO, a seven-
dataset benchmark that separates knowledge supply, policy
identification, and private-model compilation under disjoint
data roles. Controlled studies expose inflated oracle gains,
architecture-dependent transfer reversals, and a gap be-
tween teacher accuracy and private-model utility. Ordinary
public-response distillation provides a competitive reference
without public task labels or newcomer samples: gains over
strengthened local training are 23.52 and 16.62 percent-
age points on 300 CelebA identities and 300 FedEMNIST
writers, respectively. In a complete-pipeline FedEMNIST
comparison, this reference reaches 97.13% accuracy with
12.4 seconds of compilation per

A selector A chooses k∈ {0, . . . , K}using declared
onboarding evidence, with hc,0 =f c,0. Query labels Dqryc
are evaluation-only. For higher-is-better utilityU, client gain
is
Gk(c) =U(f c,k;c)−U(f c,0;c)∈[−1,1].(1)

evidence.excerpt:
Source clients train the bank; shadow (meta) clients select
policies before held-out test scoring (Table 1). Prospective
studies freeze plans before test access. Labeled revisions
reuse evaluated cohorts but make new choices on shadow-
development clients. The five-dataset policy audit repeats
optimization with five seeds and linear/deep heads; UCI
HAR uses linear models and temporal CNNs. Seeds are not
independent clients. MELD assigns modalities by speaker
and preserves dialogue separation. UCF51-20 preserves in-
divisible video groups; its clients are simulated. TCGA uses
eligible Tissue Source Sites and class-stratified 60/20/20
splits. UCI HAR withholds gyroscope from half the sub-
jects; FedEMNIST preserves writer identities and official
within-writer partitions. Cohort and freeze receipts are sup-
plementary.

evidence.excerpt:
NIST uses 4,096 images from 500 public writers to compile
unseen pixel-MLP/CNN models. Neither compiler uses pub-
lic task labels or newcomer inputs; the primary decentralized
revision removes the historical public-label progression gate.
Selectors include fixed policies, empirical selection-label
argmax,Active Testing(fixed ensemble surrogate, expected-
loss acquisition, 10% uniform floor and LURE correc-
tion [11]),PCV(one shadow-selected policy, requiring non-
negative mean gain for every shadow client), and Eq. 4.
Local wins ties; same-query oracles are diagnostic. HAR
additionally executes PeFLL-compatible generation from 12
labeled descriptors and ATP-compatible one-step entropy
adaptation from 20 unlabeled inputs [3, 20]; their supported
interfaces and references differ.

evidence.excerpt:
HAR freezes roles, missingness, five policies and budgets
before opening 12 test subjects; a shadow-only amendment
sets two fit labels per class. Fixed KD-1 gains 3.88 pp over-
all but loses 1.73 pp in linear models and gains 9.49 pp in
temporal CNNs (Fig. 3D). The paired interaction is11.21 pp
[7.57,15.17], p=.0005 by exact sign-flip. Six disagreement
labels halve harm from 16.7% to 8.3%; 24 retain that harm
and raise gain to 4.47 pp (Table 4A). Neither removes neg-
ative linear-stratum gain. Architecture routing discovered
here remains retrospective.

clients; UCF, 4 simulated silos.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Headline performance is evaluated using true ground-truth labels from held-out test splits across natural clients and writers, accompanied by client-bootstrap confidence intervals.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Task-specific target evaluation metrics (classification accuracy and balanced accuracy) scored on held-out newcomer test query sets whose labels are strictly withheld during compilation.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Response distillation loss (KL/BCE matching frozen bank teacher logits on unlabeled public anchor inputs) and local fit labels.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Reported findings closely reflect empirical results: the authors explicitly demonstrate where distillation succeeds (e.g., substantial gains on CelebA and FedEMNIST) and openly highlight where transfer fails, produces negative transfer, or causes client harm (e.g., CREMA-D and linear HAR models).
primary.evaluation_assessment: The empirical evaluation is remarkably comprehensive, testing simple public-response KD against strengthened local controls, hypernetwork generators, and test-time personalization baselines across multiple modalities. It thoroughly audits failure modes, reporting client harm rates, anchor support interventions, cost amortizations, and the hazards of same-query selection optimism.

primary.limitations: The manuscript transparently discusses key constraints, including small test cohorts for MELD/TCGA, simulated action silos, in-domain public anchors, lack of formal differential privacy guarantees, and the non-equivalence of finite sample guarantees to prospective individual safety.
primary.method_assessment: The methodology is exceptionally rigorous, strictly formalizing role-disjoint protocols (source, public anchors, shadow clients, and evaluation-only test query sets) and mathematically proving identifiability limits and mean-gain concentration certificates. Model compilation and baseline methods are carefully specified across distinct architecture types without target query label leakage.
primary.quality_rationale: This work sets a high standard for benchmarking post-federation transfer by combining theoretical grounding with scrupulously controlled experiments, pre-registered chronologies, and explicit disclosures of both positive and negative outcomes. It clearly qualifies for acceptance.
primary.scoped_contribution: FEDNBO introduces a seven-dataset benchmark and formal decomposition (supply, identification, compilation) to evaluate post-federation knowledge transfer into unseen, newcomer-chosen private architectures using disjoint data roles and declared onboarding evidence.

scholarly_quality.rationale: This work sets a high standard for benchmarking post-federation transfer by combining theoretical grounding with scrupulously controlled experiments, pre-registered chronologies, and explicit disclosures of both positive and negative outcomes. It clearly qualifies for acceptance.
